actions.action: Remove plant from pot and inspect roots and corms
Cut away rotted roots and mushy stems if present
Let plant dry out for a few hours before repotting
Dust cuts with cinnamon or fungicide if corm is firm
Repot in fresh chunky mix (2 parts soil to 1 part perlite/bark) with corm top at soil line, discarding moldy soil
Use a pot with drainage holes or a plastic nursery pot inside the metal pot
Empty water that collects in the outer pot
Cut off dead and collapsed leaves
Check top 1-2 inches of soil and water only when dry
If base is mush, start firm corm pieces in moist perlite or sphagnum moss

reason: The answer gets poor drainage and low light right, but it blames overwatering and rot when the plant was actually underwatered and root-bound. Its repotting, drainage and window-light advice overlaps with the fix, but it also says to water less. The soil-check safeguard keeps that from being harmful.
